summary.continental_ancestry: Reference individuals left out of their own panel are assigned on average at least 75% to their own continent (250,000 SNPs; 75% with 80,000). On 24 simulated genomes mixing two or three continents, built from left-out individuals' chromosomes, the proportions were within 4.8 percentage points on average (23.5 at worst), and the 95% intervals contained the true value 43% of the time.
summary.regional_ancestry: With 80,000 SNPs, people left out of the reference panels are assigned on average 76% to their own region (lowest region 50%); regions that could not be told apart were merged before the pack was built (11 merges).
summary.chromosome_painting: On simulated genomes with known ancestry segments, the pair of ancestries was right at 84% of SNPs, and the average confidence the method reported was 87%.
summary.indigenous_american: Detection limit 2.8%. On simulated genomes with known Indigenous American ancestry the proportion was recovered within 4.9 points from 5% upwards; detection rates at 2%, 5% and 10% were 0%, 100% and 100%; 0% of genomes with none, and 0% of left-out East Asian genomes, were reported as having some.
summary.roh: Segments match PLINK 1.9's --homozyg on the same genotypes (total length within 8.5%, overlap at least 0.91), and homozygous stretches of known length inserted into real genomes were found over 99% of their length.
summary.x_ancestry: From X-chromosome SNPs alone, people left out of the reference panels are assigned on average at least 61% to their own continent.
